specialty: technical soundness: are the definitions, nulls and inferences correct? Try to break the central argument.
summary: The paper argues that multiple-choice scores should be gated against the construct's best constant, input-blind predictor rather than nominal chance, that this floor is itself an estimator needing its own calibration, and that the calibrating null must be realisable by the construct. It reports nine letter-construct floors with a legality-aware balanced-null calibration (Table 1), an MMLU-Pro read-out over 17 designated damaged cells (Table 3, 15/17 at or below floor), a symmetric-standard restatement of the wrong-null flip (3/12 vs 1/12, Sec 5.1), an off-MMLU replication (9/85 vs 45/85), a stratified arm-conditional permutation null (read-out v2, Sec 3.2, Table 6) used to re-judge 27 cells, and an fp32-vs-bf16 control that removes 100% of exact ties and flips 18.03% of letter argmaxes without moving accuracy. I recomputed the central quantities from the shipped evidence and they hold: 1403/12032=0.11660572 (floor), 3776/14042=0.26890756, 2033/3270=0.62171254, the 36-item / 0.2992 pp stratified-ordering slack (1439/12032-1403/12032), the collapse-invariance self-test (always-A/E/J deltas 0.000/-2.111/-3.807 pp reproduce exactly from the per-letter gold counts), the BH step-up over m=27 (qwen3/k14 q=0.0297 rejects, olmo2/keep14 q=0.0663 does not), the binomial 0.019568 for X>=3 of 12, the truncation audit (14 cells with before/after, 8 argmax flips all on affected items, max 0.0083 pp, 0 verdict changes), and 2532/14042=18.0316%. The self-criticism is unusually disciplined: the flagship MMLU-Pro row is voluntarily withdrawn from significance (p=0.083), a rounding convention that biased p toward 'survives' is disclosed, and two ARC rows are reported as moving in the authors' favour. But the paper's own honesty exposes what I think is a fatal gap for the quantitative claim: after the legality-aware correction only two of nine rows survive, and both are trivial cases where the floor is a large gold-marginal skew (BoolQ 0.6217 vs 0.50) or a well-powered fixed-4-way skew (MMLU). The interesting rows all fail. Worse, the calibrating null is applied only to the FLOOR, never to the arm-vs-floor comparison, so the same winner's-curse the paper discovered invalidates its two headline exceptions: I measure the floor estimator's own sd at 0.245 pp under resampling at the observed label distribution, larger than the +0.233 pp qwen3/k14 margin the paper calls 'statistically real', and larger in absolute value than the -0.075/-0.158 pp cells it calls 'at floor' with 0.083 pp half-widths. There are also three concrete defects: the appendix's directional standard-error figures ('-17 and -23 standard errors', dp -0.0025/-0.0063) match no field in the cited evidence file (which records dp_sigma -3.34/-7.34 and dp -0.001205/-0.005213, with a third inconsistent set in the same file's top-level string); the reproducibility statement's mechanised-checker claim ('610 numerals, none unresolved') does not hold in the artifact, where code/check_prose_vs_evidence.py scans 0 files and reports 12/12 uncovered targets, still reading the SUPERSEDED legality-blind evidence file; and code/emit_tab_construct_nulls.py exits rc=1 on a missing dependency. Four named gate scripts and E-A/E-B/E-K's EVIDENCE_PACK.md are absent from the artifact.
strengths: The core protocol claim is correct, cleanly stated, and useful. Sec 3.1 (03_method.tex:10-18) defines f_const = max_L (1/n) sum 1[y_i=L] and makes the decision rule explicitly asymmetric: failure disqualifies, passing is necessary-not-sufficient, with feng2019misleading cited as the reason (01_introduction.tex:26). This is the right logical shape for a validity gate and is not what the 445-benchmark checklist of bean2025measuring covers.

The winner's-curse framing of the floor is a genuine and non-obvious methodological point: f_hat = max_L m_hat_L is a maximum over k noisy marginals, so a positive gap is not evidence the floor differs from chance. I verified the consequence is real and large relative to the reported gaps: three of nine rows (CommonsenseQA 0.208845, PIQA 0.504897, and effectively ARC-Challenge 0.265358) sit at or BELOW E[f_hat] (Table 1 / construct_nulls_legality_aware.json rows), which is exactly the trap the paper is warning about.

The legality-aware correction (Sec A.1.5, 03b_nulls.tex:30-41) is a real and correctly-diagnosed error in the authors' own prior calibration: a uniform-over-10 null assigns gold J to 2051/12032 MMLU-Pro items that cannot have it. I confirmed the arithmetic of the asymmetry from the shipped selftest: E[m_A]=12032/12032/10-weighted = 0.110877 vs E[m_J]=9981/120320=0.08295379, matching 03b_nulls.tex:33 to 6 dp. Reporting this against the paper's own flagship row, and withdrawing the claim rather than the null, is the correct scientific move.

The symmetric-standard restatement (Sec 5.1, 05_analysis.tex:9-23) is the single most important self-correction: applying the same paired-bootstrap CI to the chance reference collapses the advertised 10/12-vs-1/12 flip to 3/12-vs-1/12. I verified the accompanying multiplicity statement independently: BH at q=0.05 over the 12 cells retains nothing on either side, and the binomial P(X>=3 | n=12, p=0.05) = 0.019568 exactly reproduces the quoted 0.0196 (09a_relocated.tex:37). Very few papers voluntarily shrink their own headline effect by a factor of three.

The v2 constant-collapse identity is stated as an identity and verified as one. The self-test in evidence/heal_readout_v2_permutation_null.json gives delta_perm = 0.0 for all ten letters, and I independently recovered the per-letter gold counts (A 1403 ... J 945, summing to exactly 12032 with the legality-conditioned denominators) and reproduced the Sec 3.2 v1 deltas (always-A +0.000, always-E -2.111, always-J -3.807 pp) to the printed precision. The paper also correctly declines to claim the statistic (Cohen's kappa numerator) and confines its claim to the varying-k stratification (03_method.tex:36-59).

The v1/v2 ordering is honestly presented as a measured property under a stated regularity condition rather than a theorem, with the counterexample constructed: the per-stratum argmax is B,E,B,E for n_opt=5..8, giving sum_s w_s max_L m_{s,L} = 1439/12032 and a violation of exactly 36 items = 0.2992 pp, which I recomputed (09a_relocated.tex:15). The paper also says which 13 of 27 cells could not have violated the bound, so the 27/27 empirical count is not oversold.

The integrity ledger is auditable and its numbers check out. The bootstrap p=1.042 root cause in evidence/R7_BOOTSTRAP_P_FIX.md is not just asserted but reproduced bit-for-bit ((bs<=0).mean()=0.5210, (bs>=0).mean()=0.5334, sum = 1 + P(bs==0) = 1.0544, 2x0.5210=1.0420), and the truncation audit's '0/14 verdicts changed, max 0.0083 pp, all eight flips on affected items' reproduces exactly from trunc_fix_before_after.json.

The denominator fix is disclosed at the point of exclusion (09a_relocated.tex:24): an earlier version's 14/15 and 0/15 silently omitted shortgpt16 (+3.674, p=0.0001) and keep14 (+0.324, p=0.3234), and the inconsistency is named (retained depth 14 was damaged for the three non-OLMo families in the same ratio). This is exactly the failure mode a measurement paper should be held to, and they hold themselves to it.
weaknesses: FATAL FOR THE QUANTITATIVE CLAIM: the winner's-curse calibration is applied to the FLOOR but never to the ARM-VS-FLOOR comparison, and by the paper's own logic it must be. The arm's paired bootstrap (Table 3, tab_mmlupro.tex) resamples items and recomputes acc - f_const(0.116606) against a FIXED floor treated as a known constant; the shipped evidence confirms this (mmlu_pro_power_nulls_v2.json uses floor_used = 0.11660571808510638 for every cell, and construct_nulls_legality_aware.json:floor_invariance boasts that no null moment enters those counts). But Sec 1 and Table 1's caption say the floor is an ESTIMATE with its own sampling distribution. I measured that distribution at the observed label marginal (200k multinomial draws at n=12032, seed 7, per-letter counts recovered from the paper's own selftest): sd(max_L m_hat_L) = 0.245 pp, E[max_L m_hat_L] - observed = +0.055 pp, and P(argmax != A) = 0.231. Both headline exceptions are inside that: qwen3/k14 is +0.233 pp with half-width 0.191 pp (Table 3 row 11, p=0.0192), i.e. its 'statistically real' margin is smaller than ONE standard deviation of the reference it is measured against. The same objection hits the two 'significantly below floor' cells (llama2/k8 -0.914 p=0.0168; qwen3/k8 -0.881 p=0.0362, tab_v2_resort.tex rows 1-2) and every 'at floor' cell whose half-width is 0.083 pp (llama2/k12, llama2/k14). Two of the three headline exception statements in the abstract and 01_introduction.tex:21 therefore have a stated precision the design cannot deliver. This is not new-experiment work: the floor's sampling distribution is a closed-form/parametric-bootstrap quantity from the gold labels the authors already have, and the honest fix is either to state that the reported per-cell decisions are conditional on the observed floor, or to widen the intervals.

The surviving quantitative evidence is exactly the two rows where the claim is least interesting, and the paper's own scoping sentence does not concede this. Table 1 (tab_nulls.tex) leaves MMLU (fixed 4-way, floor 0.268908, n=14042) and BoolQ (fixed 2-way, floor 0.621713, gap +12.17 pp) as the only rows with p<10^-5. BoolQ's 'floor is not chance' is a well-known label imbalance, not a measurement subtlety; MMLU's +1.891 pp survives largely because n is the largest of the fixed-k set. The six rows that would have demonstrated the phenomenon at small n and at variable k are all inside the estimator's noise (p=0.083 to 0.853). The abstract calls this 'establishes that chance is the wrong reference without establishing that the floor differs from it in magnitude' -- but if the floor cannot be shown to differ from chance in magnitude on six of eight constructs, the operational payoff of gating against the floor rather than chance is unquantified precisely where the paper's own damaged-arm results live (all five off-MMLU benchmarks are among the six).

The floor's calibration test is a max-cell test where an omnibus test is the natural one, and the omnibus test is much weaker. On the same data and the same legality-aware null, I get chi-square GOF = 10.22 on 9 df, p = 0.333 (obs A..J = 1403,1352,1314,1336,1149,1128,1182,1115,1108,945 against legality-implied expectations 1334.07,...,998.10). The paper's p=0.083 for MMLU-Pro is Pr(max_L m_hat_L >= observed floor), which is the right null for the question 'could a balanced null produce a floor this high', but a reader will read it as 'the gold labels are non-uniform', and on that question the same data say p=0.33. Sec A.1.5 should state which question the p answers and give the omnibus figure alongside, otherwise the 0.083 is easy to over-read.

NUMBERS IN THE APPENDIX DO NOT MATCH THE CITED EVIDENCE. 03b_nulls.tex:37 states the two ARC rows 'move slightly in our favour, by -0.0025 and -0.0063 in p --- real rather than Monte-Carlo error at roughly -17 and -23 standard errors'. In evidence/construct_nulls_legality_aware.json, rows[ARC-Easy].directionality gives dp_aware_minus_blind = -0.001205 with dp_sigma = -3.34 (and dE_max_sigma = -9.78); rows[ARC-Challenge] gives dp = -0.005213 with dp_sigma = -7.34 (dE_max_sigma = -17.75). The SAME file's top-level 'directionality' string gives a third pair (dp = -0.004 and -0.005, 'both about -33 sigma'), and the naive p_blind - p_aware differences are -0.003999 and -0.004873. So there are four mutually inconsistent (delta-p, sigma) pairs for the same two rows, and the manuscript prints a fifth combination that appears in none of them. The manuscript's -17/-23 look like the dE_max sigmas of one row grafted onto the dp figures of another. Since this sentence exists specifically to make a directional-honesty claim auditable, it must be exactly right; as printed, a referee who checks it finds a mismatch. (The verdicts do not turn on it -- 0.140->0.136 and 0.453->0.447 -- but the epistemic point does.)

THE REPRODUCIBILITY STATEMENT'S CENTRAL MECHANISED CLAIM DOES NOT HOLD IN THE ARTIFACT. 10_reproducibility.tex:3-10 says a checker 'walks all numerals in the source and requires each to be either an exact match to a value in the evidence set... at the time of writing it reports 610 numerals with none unresolved'. Running the shipped checker in the snapshot: `python3 code/check_prose_vs_evidence.py --out /tmp/x.json` gives rc=0 but prints '[scan] 0 files, 21 targets' and '[result] n_checked=0 n_ok=0 ... n_uncovered=12', listing all nine letter floors plus two OpenBookQA content nulls and Winogrande as 'appears in no scanned file'. It scans PAPER/README.md and PAPER/sections/*.tex (check_prose_vs_evidence.py:307-308), neither of which exists in the snapshot layout (sections are under manuscript/). Independently, its target set is built from evidence/floor_winners_curse_calibration.json (line 92, CALIB) -- the file that construct_nulls_legality_aware.json explicitly SUPERSEDES -- and the word 'legality' does not appear anywhere in the checker (grep rc=1). So the checker that vouches for the paper's numbers is pointed at the retracted null. The companion emitter also fails: `python3 code/emit_tab_construct_nulls.py` exits rc=1 with FileNotFoundError on evidence/e2_single_source_assertion.json. Appendix A.9 (09_appendix.tex:56-77) claims this emitter 'refuses to write on any inconsistency' and re-verifies every number in Table 1; in the artifact it cannot run at all.

ARTIFACT INCOMPLETENESS ON LOAD-BEARING PATHS. Table 8 (tab_artifact-map, 09_appendix.tex:114-138) resolves E-A, E-B, E-F, E-K to tcodex_out/EVIDENCE_PACK.md; `find` over the snapshot returns no EVIDENCE_PACK match, so the sources for Table 1's floors (E-A), the entire MMLU-Pro per-cell table (E-B, partially covered by mmlu_scale_power/), Table 4's conventions (E-F) and the claim ledger (E-K) are not resolvable. Four gate scripts named in the prose as enforcing the paper's key invariants are absent: gate_designated_denominator.py (09a_relocated.tex:24), gate_bh_27cell_consistency.py (tab_v2_full.tex:38), plus evidence/mmlupro_legality_aware_null_MAIN.json and evidence/second_mc_benchmark_crossfamily/gate2_crossfamily_nulls.json, the latter being a hard dependency of the shipped checker (GATE2X, line 96). The 9/85 and 45/85 off-MMLU counts are not derivable from any shipped file: gate2_letter_content_nulls.json carries per-arm verdicts for six OLMo-2 arms x six tasks, not the 17-arm x 5-benchmark designated set, and grep for '9/85' or '45/85' across evidence/ returns nothing. So the abstract's third headline count is un-auditable in this snapshot.

THE POWER CLAIM USES A NON-STANDARD AND UNSTATED DEFINITION OF 'POWERED'. 04_experiments.tex:20 and the abstract say 'all 21 evaluated cells are powered at the scale of the reference effect'. The criterion in mmlu_pro_power_nulls_v2.json:power_verdict is 'achieved CI95 half-width < 1.389 pp', which is NOT statistical power. Under that criterion a cell with half-width 1.388 pp has power 0.399 against delta=1.389 at alpha=0.05, not 0.80; the half-width needed for 80% power is 0.9717 pp. MMLU-Pro's max half-width is 0.96836 pp, giving power 0.803, so the claim survives numerically for the reported cells by 0.0034 pp of margin -- but the same criterion is used in Table 5 (tab_power.tex) to label MMLU (hw 1.154), ARC-Easy (1.305) and Winogrande (1.184) as detecting the effect ('reference', 'yes, borderline', 'yes'), and I compute their actual power as 0.655, 0.550 and 0.633. The '52/60 underpowered' and '7/60 significantly below' framing (05_analysis.tex:29) inherits this. Define the criterion in the paper as 'CI half-width below the reference effect' rather than 'powered', or recompute at 80%.

THE MATERIALITY BAR IS APPLIED TO ONE CELL AND WOULD DISQUALIFY OTHERS IF APPLIED UNIFORMLY. Sec 3.2 (03_method.tex:79) requires recovery_fraction >= 0.10 x the same-family intact anchor. From evidence/heal_readout_v2_permutation_null.json I computed the ratio for every trace/upgrade cell: qwen3/k14 0.0907 (paper says 9.1%, correct, immaterial), but olmo2/keep14 -- the cell the paper promotes from 'at floor' to TRACE_SIGNAL and discusses at length (05_analysis.tex:41, tab_v2_resort.tex:12) -- has 0.02041/0.30447 = 0.0670, i.e. it fails the SAME bar more decisively than the cell the paper disqualifies, and this is never stated. shortgpt16 is 0.327 and passes. The paper does say the upgrade does not survive BH (q=0.0663, which I verified), so nothing collapses, but the asymmetric application of the materiality rule -- invoked to demote the exception that hurts the thesis, silent on the one that helps it -- is exactly the kind of selective-standard problem this paper is otherwise built to prevent.

CLAIM-LEDGER / MANUSCRIPT DRIFT. evidence/claim_evidence_map.tsv is cited as E-K and as the row-by-row source of Table 7 (tab_claims.tex caption: 'whose retracted-claim rows correspond one-to-one with the rows here'), but its C-13 row still reads 'The honest MMLU-Pro count is 14/15' while Table 7 row 13 reads 15/17, and its H-03 row still says 'NARROWED to 3 constructs... only MMLU-Pro, MMLU, BoolQ survive' -- the pre-legality-aware count that the abstract now correctly reports as two. The paper is careful to say (09_appendix.tex:56-77) that the ledger is machine-checked; here the checked artifact contradicts the manuscript on two of the paper's headline scopings.

PROTOCOL FIELD CONTRADICTS THE PROTOCOL PROSE. 04_experiments.tex:13 and 10_reproducibility.tex:15 state 'MMLU-Pro cross-family runs use maximum length 2048; every final cell has zero truncation', and Table 7 row 14 retracts the 1536 numbers. But the shipped per-cell record mmlu_pro_power_nulls_v2.json records protocol.max_len = 1536. The numbers themselves are fine -- I checked that its per-cell letter deltas equal the 'after' (2048) block of trunc_fix_before_after.json cell-for-cell (e.g. qwen3/k14 +0.2327127659574468, p=0.0192, hw 0.19115691) -- so this is a stale metadata field rather than a wrong result. It nonetheless means the only machine-readable file behind Table 3 self-describes as the retracted launch, which is a provenance hazard given that Table 7 row 14 exists specifically to prohibit those numbers. Relatedly, mmlu_pro_power_nulls.json (the v1 companion, still a cited path under evidence/mmlu_scale_power) has crossfamily = {} and power_verdict.n_cells = 6, so a reader following the cited directory can land on an empty predecessor.

PRE-REGISTRATION IS SELF-CANCELLING AS APPLIED. 03_method.tex:81-82 concedes the 27 v2 numbers are 'post-hoc by construction because those cells had already been scored, and the designer had already seen the shape of the collapse defect'. That is the right disclosure, but it means the materiality constant 0.10, the anchor-blocking rule, and the stratification were all fixed by someone who had seen which cells were near the boundary -- and the two cells the analysis turns on (qwen3/k14 at 0.0907 and llama2's blocked anchor at 0.0545) both sit within a factor of two of that constant. The paper cannot claim the rule is pre-registered for THESE cells, and Sec 3.2 should not present the constant without noting how close the decisive cells are to it.

THE NEGATIVE CONTROL IS UNDER-USED AND ITS ONE STRIKING NUMBER IS UNDISCUSSED. Winogrande is called the sole negative control (04_experiments.tex:5) but appears in only two rows of Table 4 and one of Table 5, and enters no denominator. Table 4 (tab_conventions.tex:15) shows Winogrande token-unit 'credit' = 0.933702 -- a content floor of 93% on a 2-way task, the single most vivid demonstration in the paper that a tie convention can make a null arbitrary -- and no sentence anywhere discusses it. Conversely, no floor-test outcome ON the control is reported as a control result, i.e. the paper never shows that its gate correctly declines to fire where it should not.

SCOPE OF THE DAMAGED-ARM EVIDENCE. The regime confound is disclosed repeatedly and correctly (04_experiments.tex:8, 07_limitations.tex:15), but the consequence is stronger than the paper's phrasing suggests: OLMo-2 is the ONLY prune-then-heal family, all nine off-MMLU above-floor cells are OLMo-2, and no truncation rung retains more than 14 layers (09a_relocated.tex:44). The 'regime-and-depth pattern organising its exceptions' that Sec 4 (04_experiments.tex:23) offers as the substitute for multiplicity control is therefore a single-family pattern, and its cleanest instance (shortgpt16 at 16/32 layers) has no matched comparator in any other family.
questions: Sec 5.1 / Table 3: the arm-vs-floor bootstrap holds f_const fixed at 0.116606 while Table 1's caption says the floor is a noisy estimate. Resampling items at the observed gold marginal gives sd(max_L m_hat_L) = 0.245 pp and P(argmax != A) = 0.231. Under an interval that also propagates floor uncertainty, does qwen3/k14 (+0.233, hw 0.191) remain 'above floor', and do llama2/k8 (-0.914) and qwen3/k8 (-0.881) remain 'below'? If the answer is 'the reported decisions are conditional on the observed floor', please say so explicitly at Table 3 and in the abstract's 'only two clear their best-constant floor'.

03b_nulls.tex:37 prints delta-p of -0.0025 / -0.0063 at '-17 and -23 standard errors'. The cited evidence file records dp = -0.001205 (sigma -3.34) and -0.005213 (sigma -7.34) per row, dE_max sigmas of -9.78 and -17.75, and a top-level string giving dp -0.004/-0.005 at '-33 sigma'. Which quantity and which standard error are in the manuscript sentence, and can all four be reconciled or the discrepant ones withdrawn?

The reproducibility statement claims 610 numerals checked with none unresolved. In the artifact, code/check_prose_vs_evidence.py scans 0 files (it globs PAPER/sections/*.tex and PAPER/README.md) and reports 12/12 targets uncovered, and its target set is built from the SUPERSEDED evidence/floor_winners_curse_calibration.json with no reference to the legality-aware file. Was the 610-numeral run performed with a different checker version or a different tree, and can the checker be repointed at the legality-aware evidence and re-run in the released layout?

code/emit_tab_construct_nulls.py exits rc=1 (FileNotFoundError: evidence/e2_single_source_assertion.json). Appendix A.9 says this emitter re-parses every number in Table 1 and refuses to write on inconsistency. Can the missing dependency be shipped so a reader can execute the guarantee the appendix describes?

Where are the 9/85 and 45/85 off-MMLU counts computed? gate2_letter_content_nulls.json carries six OLMo-2 arms x six tasks (36 cells, with Winogrande a control), not the 17-arm designated set x 5 benchmarks, and grep across evidence/ finds neither ratio. Please ship the per-cell 85-row record, or say which file the ratios are read from.

power_verdict's criterion is 'CI95 half-width < 1.389 pp', which corresponds to power ~0.40 at the boundary, not 0.80. Would the authors either rename the property ('half-width below the reference effect') or recompute at a stated power target? In particular Table 5 labels MMLU (hw 1.154), ARC-Easy (1.305) and Winogrande (1.184) as detecting the effect, where I compute power 0.655/0.550/0.633.

The materiality rule (>= 0.10 x same-family intact anchor) demotes qwen3/k14 at ratio 0.0907. Applied to olmo2/keep14 the ratio is 0.02041/0.30447 = 0.0670 -- a clearer failure -- yet keep14's promotion to TRACE_SIGNAL is discussed as a substantive re-sort. Should the same bar be printed for keep14, and does anything in Sec 5.3 change if it is?

evidence/claim_evidence_map.tsv (cited as E-K and as the one-to-one source of Table 7) still says '14/15' at C-13 and 'NARROWED to 3 constructs' at H-03, against the manuscript's 15/17 and two-of-eight. Which is authoritative, and can the ledger be re-emitted so the one-to-one claim holds?

mmlu_pro_power_nulls_v2.json records protocol.max_len = 1536 while the paper says every reported cross-family cell used 2048 and Table 7 row 14 prohibits the 1536 numbers. I verified the per-cell values equal the 2048 'after' block, so this looks like a stale field -- can it be corrected, and can mmlu_pro_power_nulls.json (crossfamily = {}) be removed or marked superseded so the cited directory contains no empty predecessor?

On the same data and the same legality-aware null, an omnibus chi-square GOF of the gold letter marginal gives chi2 = 10.22, df = 9, p = 0.333, against the max-cell p = 0.083. Would the authors report both, and state explicitly that the p in Table 1 answers 'could a balanced null produce a floor this high' rather than 'are these labels non-uniform'?

Table 4 reports Winogrande token-unit 'credit' = 0.933702, a 93% input-blind content floor on a 2-way task. This seems like the paper's strongest single illustration that a tie convention can make a null meaningless, yet no text discusses it. Is there a reason it is not foregrounded, and is there a floor-test outcome on the control that shows the gate correctly declining to fire?
what_would_change_my_score: TO 8: (a) propagate floor-estimator uncertainty into the arm-vs-floor comparison, or state unambiguously at Table 3, in Sec 5.1 and in the abstract that all per-cell decisions are conditional on the observed floor -- and re-examine the qwen3/k14 and the two below-floor exceptions under that statement (0 GPU: parametric bootstrap over the gold labels the authors already have); (b) fix or withdraw the '-17 and -23 standard errors' sentence at 03b_nulls.tex:37 so it matches a specific field in the cited evidence; (c) make the reproducibility statement true in the released artifact -- repoint check_prose_vs_evidence.py at the legality-aware evidence and at the actual section paths, ship emit_tab_construct_nulls.py's missing dependency, and ship EVIDENCE_PACK.md plus the two named gate scripts and the 85-cell off-MMLU record; (d) rename or recompute the 'powered' criterion; (e) print the materiality ratio for olmo2/keep14 alongside qwen3/k14; (f) re-emit claim_evidence_map.tsv so 14/15 and 'three constructs' no longer contradict the manuscript. All six are writing/bookkeeping/CPU-recompute, hence the ceiling of 8 without new experiments. TO 5 OR BELOW: if the floor-uncertainty issue turns out to be unfixable without new data AND the authors decline to condition the claim, because then the abstract's 'only two clear their best-constant floor' and 'qwen3/k14 is statistically real' assert a precision the design does not support; or if the 9/85 and 45/85 counts cannot be tied to a shipped record, since one of three headline flip statistics would then be unverifiable.
blindness_breach_observed: No author-side notes, target scores, or instructions about what to conclude were found in the snapshot. The .tex files contain build/provenance comments (main.tex:25-44, 03b_nulls.tex:1-4, 09a_relocated.tex:1-3, 09_appendix.tex:3-8) that reference internal paths (paperC/C9_APPLIED_20260816.md, paperC/gate/venue_page_limit.json) and explain page-budget relocations; these are ordinary LaTeX housekeeping and carry no steering. Two items are borderline and I report them for transparency rather than as breaches: (1) evidence/construct_nulls_legality_aware.json contains reviewer-process metadata in its 'why' field ('four of six round_04 blind reviewers (X1/X2/X5/X6) independently flagged...'), which reveals that this is a revision of a previously reviewed draft and how many prior reviewers raised a specific point; (2) the same file's 'directionality' and 'headline' fields contain normative instructions to the authors ('must not be printed', 'It must NOT be described as "well inside"'). Neither tells a reviewer what to conclude, and I formed the weaknesses above from my own recomputation; I did not treat the count of prior reviewers as evidence about severity. I read nothing outside submission_complete/ and used no GPU.
